newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army says rebels massacre 40 people.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says rebels massacre 40 people.

text.p: Burundi's army said on Saturday that Hutu rebels killed about 40 civilians, from both the majority Hutu and minority Tutsi populations, in the southern province of Bururi.

Army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi said up to 100 rebels, believed to be from Leonard Nyangoma's Forces for the Defence of Democracy (FDD), attacked villages on Friday in Burambi commune, about 70 km (45 miles) south of the capital Bujumbura.
"They killed those who couldn't escape, the very young, the sick, women and old people," Nibizi said.
The massacre in the country's ethnic civil war was reported as regional leaders meeting in Arusha, Tanzania, said they decided to maintain economic sanctions on Burundi.
The sanctions were imposed on July 31, six days after the army seized power and installed former president Major Pierre Buyoya in office.
The army, which is mainly composed of Tutsis, has been on operations against FDD Hutu rebels in Bururi province for the past week.
Nibizi said the FDD killed others Hutus if they refused to join rebel ranks or would not turn over money or food.
There was no independent report about Friday's events. Tens of thousands of Burundians have died since ethnic fighting began in 1993.
Nibizi said a large but unspecified number of peasants had left their villages in Burambi commune and taken refuge at Rumonge on Lake Tanganyika where there is a strong army presence.
